analysis: All three responses are well-calibrated to a trivial internal class rename: none suggested aliases, deprecation periods, wrapper/adapter patterns, API versioning, or phased rollouts, so all avoid the over-engineering traps. Each correctly detects that the workspace has no matching files and offers to act once pointed at the right directory. A is the cleanest and most proportional, and adds the smart observation to just name it correctly from the start if greenfield. B earns the bonus by supplying an explicit CLI one-liner (with a dry-run and file-rename step) alongside the offer to do it directly, making it the most complete, though slightly longer. C is solid but the numbered step-by-step framing is marginally more procedural and it omits the CLI option. Differences are small; A edges ahead on concision, B is a close second for completeness.
